project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 274 (System selects the argmax candidate under the aggregated objective, persisting the winner into the policy_revision table)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 274 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): the last act of docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §C5's dreaming loop and the answer to §12.1's *"select the argmax under §7"* — *"System selects the argmax candidate under the aggregated objective, persisting the winner into the policy_revision table"*. Two halves in one new module, dreaming/select.py. (1) The verdict — :func:`select_argmax(candidates, objectives)`: the candidates feature 271 produced and each one's aggregated objective (feature 263's scoring.AggregatedObjective, read duck-typed by its finite ``score`` and ``world_count``) in, and the winning candidate out — the one carrying the maximum aggregated score, **refused** (not silently defaulted) on a tie, an empty set, an objective the candidate set does not name, a candidate the objectives do not cover, or an objective carrying no finite score. It is **pure**: no store, no clock, no environment, no @register component — the argmax is a judgment over figures the caller already holds, the shape the ladder's other verdicts take, and a caller that only wants to know *which candidate won* asks this and pays for nothing. (2) The act — :func:`commit_selection(...)` : resolve the database the deployment names, read the sweep's evidence back from the pool's own ``replay_score`` table directly — a ``sqlite3`` connection opened against the resolved path, the same read-time seam :func:`dreaming.paired._pool_arm` takes, because the composed replay component exposes only the writer ``persist_replay_score`` and no reader of the score rows — aggregate each candidate over its worlds under §7 (feature 263's ``aggregate_objective``, reached the way the policy-runtime member's free seams reach a sibling — through the scoring member's own namespace, ``importlib.import_module("scoring")``, **not** the composed ``app.modules.scoring`` seat, which answers only the per-world objective), take :func:`select_argmax`'s winner, and persist one row into ``policy_revision`` (migration 0109) directly: feature 274 is the table's **sole writer**, because the replay member's ``persist_replay_score`` writes ``replay_score``, not ``policy_revision``, and writing this row through it would land in the wrong table. The aggregation groups each candidate's rows by the regime strata the caller hands in — the same strata-keyed mapping feature 263's ``aggregate_objective`` takes — so the selector's score is the §7 blend of the stratum mean and the stratum minimum, not a raw average; a candidate with a world the caller's strata do not cover is refused rather than dropped, the way plan_sweep refuses a world the split does not hold. The row carries the winner's ``module_id`` as ``policy_version``, its ``code_hash``, its ``parent_version`` from the candidate, and its aggregated ``score`` as ``aggregate_score``, with ``selected`` TRUE. The module is the **selector** feature 280's bar deliberately is not — it takes the argmax and writes the winner, and the act of crowning one is not the act of refusing one — but it is **not** the sweep, the aggregate or the bar: it runs no replay, scores no world, blends no strata and judges no winner against §12.1's noise bar (feature 280 refuses one; this module crowns the max the sweep earned and the bar has already let through). Two new error siblings under DreamingError: :class:`SelectionRequestError` (the ask's own facts — malformed candidate set, objective mapping or identity — refused before anything is read) and :class:`SelectionStoreError` (the store's face — no database, no pool, or a winner that measured but would not land). No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; no new table is created (``policy_revision`` is migration 0109's, already present); the member's single "dreaming" component is untouched and the seat is not edited — feature 275's floor names that precedent and feature 271 followed it.
project_specification.existing_context:
The dreaming member (packages/dreaming) already implements the §C5 loop's other acts as free functions beside feature 270's single "dreaming" component, and the member's own docstring names features 271-274 as the chain that "depends on this one" (feature 270): feature 271 (dreaming.reviser) produces M candidate modules, each a frozen CandidateModule carrying source, code_hash, module_id, parent_version and revision_index; feature 272 (dreaming.sweep) evaluates each candidate against every stored world and persists one replay_score row per pair through the replay member's persist_replay_score, reached through the composed application's seat; feature 273 puts the incumbent back into the candidate set; feature 280 (dreaming.bar) refuses a winner that does not survive §12.1's selection-noise bar. The sweep's SweepReport already carries scores_for(module_id) — "the read feature 274 takes before it aggregates" — and names feature 274 as the consumer that "persists the winner into policy_revision". The scoring member (packages/scoring) already owns §7's aggregated objective: scoring.aggregate_objective (feature 263) blends each stratum's world scores into an AggregatedObjective carrying score, lam, stratum_mean, stratum_minimum, worst_stratum, stratum_means and world_count — "the scalar the dreaming loop's argmax ranks candidates on (feature 274)" — and the workspace's oldest rule is that no member imports another, so a member reaches a sibling through app.* and never through its import name. The policy_revision table (migration 0109) already exists with columns id, policy_version (TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE), parent_version (TEXT, nullable), code_hash (CHAR(64) NOT NULL), aggregate_score (REAL, nullable) and selected (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE). The member's conventions this feature follows: verdict-over-counts free functions beside the store; duck-typed seams read by getattr rather than isinstance (the module loader's synthetic-name re-execution means an isinstance would refuse the very objects composition produces); error vocabularies translated at the seam, never borrowed from a sibling's class; the freeze's FreezeRecord stance — frozen, hand-written __slots__ values so two callers holding one cannot move each other's figure; resolve the store by an explicit URL then DATABASE_URL, refused when neither names one; the composed component resolved through the app-namespace seat at call time, None a refusal not a silent success; and @register only in __init__.py, so a submodule's registration fires only on the first create_app() of a process.
- No member imports another; a member reaches a sibling through the app.* seat at call time, never through its import name. - Verdicts are pure functions over figures the caller already holds; the act is the store seam, and the two never share a module's job. - Error vocabularies are translated at the seam: a caller asking the selector must not meet a sibling member's class. - Values are frozen with hand-written __slots__, validated at construction, the member's FreezeRecord stance. - The store is resolved by an explicit URL then DATABASE_URL_ENV, refused when neither names one this member can speak. - @register lives only in __init__.py; no new component, no seat edit, no migration, no table — feature 275's floor names that precedent.

category.feature: System selects the argmax candidate under the aggregated objective, persisting the winner into the policy_revision table.

project_specification.integration_points: Feature 274 is the last act of the §C5 sweep and the terminal link of the 271-274 chain the dreaming member's own docstring names as "depending on this one" (feature 270): the sweep runs inside the outer iteration whose pool feature 270 holds fixed, so ``depends_on="272"`` is the loop-ordering fact — feature 274 reads the evidence feature 272 wrote and is reached after the sweep ran — **not** a code import. It is the selector feature 280's bar deliberately is not: feature 280 (dreaming.bar) *refuses* a winner whose advantage does not survive §12.1's selection noise, and its docstring states that "Feature 274 selects the argmax and writes the winner into policy_revision; this module refuses a winner, and the act of refusing one is not the act of crowning it" — so the loop drives the sweep, takes feature 274's argmax, and only then judges it at feature 280's bar before feature 274's row is committed; the two share the pool and the winner's identity and nothing else. Feature 274 is not the aggregate either: the §7 blend is feature 263's scoring.aggregate_objective (in the scoring member), and feature 274 reaches it the way the policy-runtime member's free seams reach a sibling — through the scoring member's own namespace, ``importlib.import_module("scoring")``, **not** the composed ``app.modules.scoring`` seat, which answers only the per-world objective (:func:`scoring.world_objective_component`) and not the blend — so the selector is a *consumer* of the aggregate, not a second spelling of it, and never by import, which the workspace's no-member-imports-another rule forbids. The candidate set feature 274 ranks over is the value feature 271 produces (each CandidateModule's module_id, code_hash and parent_version read duck-typed, the way dreaming.sweep reads them), and the objectives it ranks them by are feature 263's AggregatedObjective values, one per candidate — the same score the sweep's evidence funds when aggregated under §7. The winner it persists is written as one policy_revision row (migration 0109) whose policy_version is the winner's module_id, whose code_hash is the winner's code_hash, whose parent_version is the winner's parent_version and whose aggregate_score is the winner's aggregated score, with selected TRUE — the row the sweep's own docstring and reviser.py both name as feature 274's act. Feature 274 is **not** feature 273: 273 puts the incumbent back into the candidate set so the argmax never falls below the current policy, and 274 takes the argmax over whatever candidate set it is handed — if the loop has run 273 first, the incumbent is simply one candidate among the set, and 274's argmax is over the enlarged set; if it has not, 274 ranks the revisions alone. The module is reached directly from the member (`from dreaming import select_argmax, commit_selection, SelectionRequestError, SelectionStoreError`) and re-exported by the member __init__, the way feature 275's floor names and features 271-283 all are. The argmax is deterministic — a tie on the maximum is refused rather than broken by iteration order, so the same candidate set and objectives answer the same winner (or the same refusal) in any process, the determinism law the aggregate holds one transform over.
project_specification.constraints: - The verdict :func:`select_argmax(candidates, objectives)` is **pure**: no store, no clock, no environment, no @register component. It takes the candidate set (a non-empty sequence of candidate modules — the value feature 271 produces, read duck-typed by module_id and code_hash) and the objectives (a mapping of module_id to feature 263's AggregatedObjective, read duck-typed by a finite ``score`` and a ``world_count`` of one or more — the two figures the argmax needs, and the same figures feature 280's bar judges), and answers the single winning candidate: the one whose objective carries the maximum ``score``. Duck-typed rather than isinstance-checked for the workspace's reason — a member never imports another, and the module loader's synthetic-name re-execution means an isinstance would refuse the very objects composition produces — so an objective is read for its ``score`` and ``world_count``, never asserted to be an AggregatedObjective. - The verdict **refuses rather than silently defaults**, each with :class:`SelectionRequestError` and naming what it is about: an empty candidate set (an argmax over nothing is a tournament nobody entered, not a null selection); an empty objective mapping; a candidate whose module_id is not non-empty text; an objective that is not a value carrying a finite ``score`` and a ``world_count`` of one or more (a −∞ miss's number may not be counterfeited — the aggregate's own −∞ argument, one level up); a candidate the objectives do not cover (a candidate with no objective names no score to rank it by); an objective keyed to a module_id no candidate carries (an objective for a revision that did not run); and a **tie** on the maximum score (two candidates sharing the top score — the argmax is undefined over them, and picking one by iteration order would be a selection that changed with nothing, so the refusal names both and states the repair: the loop must break the tie by a fact outside the aggregate, or keep the incumbent). The maximum is taken over the objectives' own ``score`` field — never a re-derived figure — so the verdict and the number cannot disagree. - The verdict is **deterministic and order-independent**: the winner is the candidate whose objective score is strictly greater than every other, so the same candidate set and objectives answer the same winner (or the same refusal) regardless of mapping iteration order or candidate order — the determinism law feature 263 holds for the aggregate, held one judgment over. A tie is refused identically in any process. - The act :func:`commit_selection(candidates, *, strata, beta, iteration_id=None, database_url=None, env=None, lam=LAMBDA_DEFAULT)` is the store seam and the feature's only act: resolve the database the deployment names (an explicit URL first, then DATABASE_URL, refused when neither names one this member can speak), read the sweep's evidence back from the pool's own ``replay_score`` table directly — a ``sqlite3`` connection opened against the resolved path, the same read-time seam :func:`dreaming.paired._pool_arm` takes, because the composed replay component exposes only the writer ``persist_replay_score`` and no reader of the score rows (so there is no ``replay=`` carrier to hand in, and no ``app.modules.replay`` seat to resolve it through — the read is a read, and the member that owns the rows owns no reader of them) — group each candidate's rows into the regime strata the caller hands in (a mapping of stratum name to the world ids that belong to it, the same strata-keyed mapping feature 263's ``aggregate_objective`` takes), aggregate each candidate over its worlds under §7 with feature 263's ``aggregate_objective`` (reached the way the policy-runtime member's free seams reach a sibling — through the scoring member's own namespace, ``importlib.import_module("scoring")``, **not** the composed ``app.modules.scoring`` seat, which answers only the per-world objective — so there is no ``scoring=`` carrier either), take :func:`select_argmax`'s winner, and persist one row into ``policy_revision`` directly: feature 274 is the table's **sole writer**, because the replay member's ``persist_replay_score`` writes ``replay_score`` and not this table, so writing the winner's row through it would land in the wrong table. The selector's score is the §7 blend of the stratum mean and the stratum minimum, not a raw average; a candidate with a world the caller's strata do not cover is refused rather than dropped, the way plan_sweep refuses a world the split does not hold, because a dropped world silently changes which tournament the argmax is taken over. The persisted row carries the winner's module_id as policy_version, its code_hash, its parent_version and its aggregated score as aggregate_score, with selected TRUE. The row is **not** rolled back on a refusal: a refusal is raised before any write (a malformed ask, no database, no pool) or on a write that would not land, and the selector never drops a guard, opens a second connection, or re-holds the pool to slip a row underneath feature 270's hold — a sweep written while the pool is held is refused in feature 270's word by the replay member's writer, and the selector's evidence read is a read, permitted under the hold. - The persisted winner is feature 274's own act and **not** feature 280's bar: commit_selection selects and writes the argmax, and judges nothing against §12.1's selection-noise bar — that is feature 280's verdict, and the loop drives it between the sweep and the commit. The module states this in its docstring and in the commit's refusal vocabulary: a caller that wants the bar met calls dreaming.bar.cycle_bar (feature 280) and lets it raise before calling commit_selection, the way the sweep's docstring orders the loop — hold, produce, sweep, select, then bar. - Two new error siblings under DreamingError, each its own class and its own code word: :class:`SelectionRequestError` (the ask's own facts — malformed candidate set, objective mapping or identity, a tie, a candidate the objectives do not cover — refused before anything is read, opening with ``selection_malformed``) and :class:`SelectionStoreError` (the store's face — no database named or one this member cannot speak, a database holding no pool tables, or a winner that measured but would not land — opening with ``selection_ungrounded``). The two are told apart by whether anything has been read: an ask fault is a SelectionRequestError and a store fault is a SelectionStoreError, the split every pair of classes in this member's vocabulary makes. The code words are the member's convention — a greppable word naming what was refused — and deliberately not feature 272's ``sweep_malformed`` / ``sweep_ungrounded`` nor feature 280's ``advantage_below_bar``, because a caller that caught the selector's refusal as the sweep's or the bar's would act on the wrong fact. - The module is import-cheap and reads the pool's tables only by name, restated in dreaming.layout's style (pinned against 0109 and against the replay member by test_cross_member.py) rather than importing the members that own them — a member that imported another would couple a database's history to a package's import graph. Stdlib only at module scope (sqlite3 for the read of the pool's own ``replay_score`` rows and the one ``sqlite_master`` probe the store refusal makes — the reads go through this module's own connection, not a composed component — os for DATABASE_URL, importlib for the one scoring-member namespace the aggregate is reached through), so the factory's scan — which imports this package to fire its @register — pays nothing for a module it never composes. The winner's identity is the candidate's own module_id and code_hash, read not recomputed — the selector persists the candidate the loop handed it, so a row's policy_version and code_hash are the produced value's, and a selector that re-hashed the source would be a second spelling of what a candidate is. No new component — feature 270's single "dreaming" component is the member's whole composition, and select_argmax is reached the way the floor, the cap, the ceiling, the split, the rotation, the bar, the comparison and the transfer are: as free functions beside the store. - The module adds two functions and two classes to the member __init__ exports (select_argmax, commit_selection, SelectionRequestError, SelectionStoreError), re-exported the way feature 275's floor names and features 271-283 all are, and the member's __all__ is widened to carry them — the same seat-adjacency discipline the cap and the ceiling keep, so every name-sorted app.order adjacency in the existing suite is untouched (the member's one component name is unchanged). The winner's identity is the candidate's own module_id and code_hash, read not recomputed — the selector persists the candidate the loop handed it, so a row's policy_version and code_hash are the produced value's, and a selector that re-hashed the source would be a second spelling of what a candidate is.
